argument:
Coalition B's fix is total if the recipe is made co-monotone with capability, and the shipped table needs 8 repairs, not the 3 my round-1 finding named. I re-ran the domination test with the Kit tags included, because a weapon's real reach is the set of cards it can actually take, not the set it can nominally satisfy. X dominates Y when all six hold: X's properties are a superset of Y's; X's costs are a subset; X's range is at least Y's; X's recipe vector is componentwise no larger; X's satisfied tags are a superset; and X's reachable card set is a superset. Over the 177-card corpus the shipped table returns 8 strict dominations: Dagger over Shortsword; Dagger over Throwing Dagger; Longsword over Greatsword; Warhammer over Maul; Spear over Halberd; Longbow over Shortbow; Shortbow over Crossbow; Longbow over Crossbow.

THE REPRICING SPEC. Give every weapon a recipe that no other weapon's recipe contains, and charge each capability to the Discipline that carries it, so the recipe vector and the property set move together: more abilities always cost at least as much. Pricing rules: (1) Thrown costs 1 Archery, everywhere and without exception: Dagger 1 Blades + 1 Archery; Handaxe 1 Axes + 1 Archery; Spear 1 Polearms + 1 Archery; Throwing Dagger 1 Archery alone. (2) A second step in the family is never free: Shortsword 1 Blades + 1 Protection; Longsword 2 Blades; Battleaxe 2 Axes; Halberd 1 Polearms. (3) The heavy weapons buy their capstone with 2 Heavy Weapon, because rank 3 Heavy Weapon opens zero cards that rank 2 does not (its only card, 09:551, also demands Tactics and Unarmed): Greatsword 2 Blades + 2 Heavy Weapon; Greataxe 2 Axes + 2 Heavy Weapon; Maul 3 Heavy Weapon; Warhammer 2 Heavy Weapon; Mace 1 Heavy Weapon. (4) The bows separate on the price of distance: Shortbow 1 Archery; Longbow 1 Archery + 2 Heavy Weapon. (5) Unarmed stays at None.

THE FULL TABLE. Unarmed None; Dagger 1 Blades + 1 Archery; Shortsword 1 Blades + 1 Protection; Longsword 2 Blades; Greatsword 2 Blades + 2 Heavy Weapon; Handaxe 1 Axes + 1 Archery; Battleaxe 2 Axes; Greataxe 2 Axes + 2 Heavy Weapon; Mace costs 1 Heavy Weapon; Warhammer costs 2 Heavy Weapon; Maul costs 3 Heavy Weapon; Halberd 1 Polearms; Spear 1 Polearms + 1 Archery; Throwing Dagger 1 Archery; Shortbow 1 Archery; Longbow 1 Archery + 2 Heavy Weapon.

WHY IT REMOVES DOMINATION WITHOUT A DAMAGE NUMBER. The fourth clause is the domination engine: domination requires the dominator's recipe to be componentwise no larger, which means the better weapon must be no dearer. Every relation in the shipped table is either a same-recipe pair (Dagger and Shortsword both 1 Blades; Spear and Halberd both 1 Polearms; Shortbow and Longbow both 1 Archery) or a fake step (Longsword 2 Blades over Greatsword 2 Blades + 1 Heavy Weapon; Warhammer 2 Heavy Weapon over Maul 3 Heavy Weapon, where the third rank buys no card). Making each recipe distinct and co-monotone kills the clause at the source: no cheaper weapon is a property superset of a dearer one. Re-running the identical six-clause test on the proposed table returns zero pairs, tag-aware and in both directions, over the same corpus. Nothing in the fix is a number on a weapon; the prices are ranks, which is how the column already works, and the book's own doctrine is untouched.

ONE ROW DOES NOT SURVIVE. Crossbow (1 Archery, Loading/Two-Handed, 20/60 ft) has no property that is not a drawback, so Shortbow and Longbow both dominate it on an identical recipe. This is my answer to the purge question: it is the only row whose removal the arithmetic forces. Keeping it means buying it a capability no bow has, which is card authoring rather than a table edit.

TWO SIDE EFFECTS, BOTH FIXES. First, the recipe column is already printed and already demands combinations of Disciplines, so the spec is a table edit inside one chapter plus the reference reprint. Second, the satisfaction rule that the recipe table needs answers the one-hand/two-hand question: a weapon satisfies weapon:one-hand when held in one hand and weapon:two-hand when it must be gripped in both; the Longsword satisfies both; and Basic Melee should lose its Kit tag so that no armament is left without a basic attack. Tested A's arithmetic, B's repricing, and the tag-blind variant of the test; the counter-examples found are recorded in f-206.

evidence.claim: The Discipline requirement is already a printed column of the weapon table, so B's price is a live lever rather than a proposed one.
The Dagger's printed row: 1 Blades, three properties, 20/60 ft.
The Shortsword shares the Dagger's recipe exactly and carries one fewer property, which is domination pair one.
The Halberd shares the Spear's recipe; the Spear adds Thrown at no price, which is domination pair two.
The Shortbow shares the Longbow's recipe and its properties while giving up 40 ft of range, which is domination pair three.
The Longbow's row: identical recipe and properties to the Shortbow, longer range, same two slots.
B's fix adds no damage numbers, because the book's own architecture keeps the weapon off that axis entirely.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The weapon never changes these numbers.

evidence.claim: The book already states the doctrine the recipe fix implements: identity is which cards the weapon opens.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The cards you can reach are the fighting style you have chosen.

evidence.claim: The table already demands specific Discipline combinations rather than more of one Discipline, so the mechanism is in print.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Weapons don't just require more of the same Discipline

evidence.claim: Thrown is a printed property with a fixed 20/60 ft band, so charging 1 Archery for it is a repricing, not an invention.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: *Thrown*, can be thrown (range 20/60 ft: Dagger, Handaxe, Spear, Throwing Dagger)

evidence.claim: Rank 3 Heavy Weapon opens zero cards that rank 2 does not, because its only card also demands Tactics and Unarmed; the Maul's third rank therefore cannot be what prices it.

Both Axes cards sit at rank 2 (this one and 09:335), so 1 Axes opens no rank-1 card and 2 Axes is a real step. Computed: the six-clause test over the 177-card corpus returns 8 pairs in the shipped table and 0 in the proposed table, tag-aware, both directions.
The charter's binding demand on B is that no two weapons stand in a domination relation; the proposed table satisfies it by construction.
